Q: node-gyp error Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use A:

I installed 2022 Build Tools in default location, but node-gyp complains that it can't find Visual Studio. I have tried to set VCINSTALLDIR and msvs_version with no luck.

I entered the find-visualstudio.js which throws error, add console.log(message) in the addLog (message) { ... } function to see what happened.

I got:

msvs_version not set from command line or npm config
VCINSTALLDIR not set, not running in VS Command Prompt
could not use PowerShell to find Visual Studio 2017 or newer, try re-running with '--loglevel silly' for more details.

        Failure details: undefined
unknown version "undefined" found at "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community"
checking VS2022 (17.14.36811.4) found at:
"C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools"
- found "Visual Studio C++ core features"
- missing any VC++ toolset
could not find a version of Visual Studio 2017 or newer to use
not looking for VS2017 as it is only supported up to Node.js 21
...
Error: Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use
  • Seems node-gyp found my VS installation but it lacks of components.
  • I actually set msvs_version=2022 in .npmrc, idk why it can't read it.

Then I added MSVC v143 - VS2022 x64/x86 buildtools (Latest) in Visual Studio Installer

And got:

- found "Visual Studio C++ core features"
- found VC++ toolset: v143
- missing any Windows SDK

Then I added Windows11 SDK (10.0.26100.7175)

And got:

... 
error MSB8040: Spectre-mitigated libraries are required for this project. 
Install them from the Visual Studio installer (Individual components tab) for any toolsets and architectures being used. ...

Then I added MSVC v143 - VS 2022 C++ x64/x86 Spectre-mitigated libs (Latest)

Finally it works!

Q: How to get the date of when the user was added to group? A:

Event logs might save you.

4728/4729 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-enabled global group
4732/4733 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-enabled local group
4756/4757 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-enabled universal group
4751/4752 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-disabled global group (distribution list)
4746/4747 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-disabled local group (distribution list)
4761/4762 > A member was added/removed to/from a security-disabled universal group (distribution list)

Get-EventLog -logname security | Where-Object {($_.eventid -eq 4732) -or ($_.eventid -eq 4733 ) -or ($_.eventid -eq 4746)} | select EventID,MachineName,EntryType,Message,InstanceId,TimeGenerated,Timecreated,UserName | fl | export-csv -path C:\logs.csv

Q: Access custom object in JavaScript module from another module? A:

If you have two separate HTML pages, localStorage would be the easiest solution. You can stringify your objects before placing them into localStorage.

On your first page you can do something like this to set the tree:

localStorage.setItem("avlTree", JSON.stringify(tree));

And on the second page you can do something like this to read it:

const tree = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("avlTree"));

Q: 16 kb memory page size in flutter A:

Yes, based on the llvm-readelf output you provided, your application is currently compatible with 16 KB page sizes.

Technical Breakdown:

  • Alignment Requirement: To support 16 KB pages, the ELF segments in your shared libraries (.so files) must be aligned to at least 16 KB (0x4000) or a larger power of 2 (like 64 KB / 0x10000).

  • Your Results: * Your libflutter.so and most libapp.so files show an alignment of 0x10000 (64 KB).

    • The 32-bit version (armeabi-v7a) shows 0x4000 (16 KB).

  • Why it works: Since all your libraries are aligned to at least 0x4000, they will load correctly on Android devices configured with 16 KB page sizes.

Important Note: Flutter officially started supporting 16 KB page sizes in newer versions (stable 3.24+). In your pubspec.yaml, you are using SDK ^3.8.1 (likely a typo or a dev/master version, as 3.27 is the current stable range), which definitely includes these fixes.

Recommendation: Keep ndkVersion = "28.x.x" as you have in your build.gradle.kts, as newer NDKs handle this alignment by default. You should also ensure that any third-party native plugins you add in the future are also compiled with 16 KB alignment support.

Uptade...

Since the APK Analyzer isn't working for you, here are the two most objective ways to verify 16 KB compatibility:

1. The Command Line Test (Most Reliable)

Use the zipalign tool included in the Android SDK Build-Tools. Run this command:

Bash

zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4 your_app.apk

  • Success: If it ends with "Verification successful", your APK is correctly aligned for 16 KB.

  • Failure: If it says "Verification FAILED", the alignment is incorrect.
